target_source: Independent practice: choose a substitution and complete an indefinite integral, returning an antiderivative in x. The target includes recognizing the inner function and differential.

Independent practice simplifies trig sum/difference expressions using previously learned identities. No easy examples were imported; numerical calibration may be authored without changing the operation.
Solve the displayed two-equation coefficient system, then give the coefficient sum. Example 2a+b=7, a−b=2 gives a+b=4. Radio answers are numerical.
Inspect three matrices independently and choose every diagonal matrix. A=diag(1,2), B=[[1,1],[0,2]], C=diag(3,4) has answer A+C. Current checkbox contract requires at least one qualifying choice.
Determine rank from matrix dimensions and nonpivot count on feasible ordinary matrices. A 4×7 matrix with3 nonpivot columns has rank4; full-row-rank cases belong to the target.
Evaluate definite linear-argument trig integrals using the taught antiderivative/bounds method or a justified efficient equivalent. Valid cancellations are within scope.
Integrate cos(3−2x), practicing inner-derivative scaling. The source teaches the direct primitive and does not require argument reversal/parity conversion as an answer-recognition step.

From x=t,y=t² and t=−1,0,1, calculate coordinates and choose the matching curve. The student must distinguish y=x² from y=x²+1 at the displayed answer-card size. Solution overlays may show calculated points after answering.
For u=(1,2), choose all perpendicular vectors among A=(2,−1),B=(1,1),C=(−4,2). Independently apply the dot-product criterion to each option.

A newly invented unit blick equals24cm. Convert3 blick/min to cm/s. Assess choosing factors and calculation; minute-to-second recall is a prerequisite, while the invented unit definition is a necessary given.
Find rectangle area from two supplied side lengths. Recall/select the area relationship; keep a consistent calculator and precision contract. Authored difficulty is not empirical calibration.
